subject: VectorHealth: Follow-through sprint & ownership playbook (latency incident)
messages:
From: Marcus Green <m.green@vectorhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: VectorHealth SRE <sre@vectorhealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T09:14:00Z
Subject: Urgent: Friday impact — inference latency & elevated 5xx rates

Marissa —

We saw a wide customer impact Friday night (18:46–19:35 UTC) on our payment verification pipeline. Median latency spiked from ~180ms to ~1.8s and 5xx error rate climbed to ~4.8% for the 00:30–01:00 UTC window. This affected ~12% of our traffic and triggered downstream retries that doubled our downstream latencies.

This is high severity for us — we need an initial root cause, what protections you put in place immediately, and a clear remediation plan and owners. Our SREs are available for a bridge if useful. Please escalate internally as needed.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Green
Head of Platform Engineering
VectorHealth

Date: 2028-04-10T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: Friday impact — inference latency & elevated 5xx rates

Marcus —

Thanks for the flag and sorry for the impact — we take this seriously. Immediate notes:
- We rolled a temporary configuration change at 19:05 UTC to pin requests from your project to a lower-concurrency model variant and disabled some aggressive batching heuristics for tails. That reduced observed 5xxs to ~0.6% by 19:20 UTC.
- We opened a short-lived capacity burst and increased autoscaling response until midnight to avoid recurrence while we investigate.

Neha and Markus are on the technical RCA; I will coordinate exec updates and credit discussions. Can we do a 30-min bridge today at 16:00 UTC to go over the initial findings and next steps?

Attaching an action tracker (starter) — we'll populate owners and deadlines after the bridge.

Sincerely,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Green <m.green@vectorhealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T08:37:00Z
Subject: Initial technical findings — VectorHealth latency incident (root cause hypothesis)

Marissa / Marcus / Markus —

Summary (TL;DR):
- Primary contributor: KV-cache sharding imbalance in the hot keyspace combined with a new kernel selection path that deferred a quantized-kernel fallback, which increased CPU contention and token-level latency for a subset of long-sequence requests.
- Secondary contributor: A recent batching heuristic change (introduced 2028-03-27) increased tail-aggregation windows for low-frequency prefixes used by your workflow; that amplified the latency spike during the traffic surge.
- Mitigation we applied: disabled the new heuristic and forced the quantified kernel fallback for the impacted model family; warmed KV-cache and reduced default batch-window for your project.

Next actions (proposed sprint plan):
1) (24h) Patch to enforce deterministic KV-shard mapping for hot keys — owner: markus_klein — due: 2028-04-12 23:59 UTC.
2) (72h) Revert and rework batching heuristic with A/B canary and telemetry gating — owner: neha_kapoor — due: 2028-04-14 23:59 UTC.
3) (7d) Comprehensive kernel-selection safety net to avoid delayed fallbacks — owner: infra-kernel-team (tracked SUP-9012) — due: 2028-04-19.
4) (30d) Add prefix-aware caching and SLO-specific autoscale tuning for VectorHealth routes — owner: marissa_cole (coordination) — due: 2028-05-10.

I've attached a short root cause summary and the action tracker with proposed owners. We'll discuss on the 16:00 UTC bridge.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Reliability
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Thanks for the quick analysis and the bridge earlier — that was helpful. A few asks from our side before we put this in our operational schedule:

- Please provide a tight timeline and a single point of contact for weekly checkpoints until the 30-day deliverables are closed.
- Any plan changes that could impact query semantics (e.g., quantization fallback behavior) must be flagged to our SREs and signed off.

I'll route the credit ask to LegalOps and Finance; cc'ing them. We appreciate the owners and immediate mitigations.

—Marcus
